uncovered-rendered-later.undoes: C — when a reading would leave the bars with a stretch the marks on the page do not cover, the new marks are rendered before the observer or the event returns (the step 9-D review, D-01)

margin-a-bar-length.undoes: C — the marks reach a capped margin past the bars, not a whole bar's length (the step 9-D review, D-03)

scrollbars-not-content.undoes: C (step 9-E, E-01) — the content reaches over the scrollbars that take space and a box's fractional width

margin-300.undoes: C (step 9-E, E-04; step 9-F, F-03) — the margin covers a sidebar hiding while zoomed in, where the canvas's content goes from wider than its box to centred

flush-in-commit.undoes: C (step 9-E, E-03) — a reading taken in React's commit is not flushed there

flush-in-commit.unguarded: jsdom never reaches it: its layout stub puts no uncovered reading in the zoom's layout effect (step 9-E, E-05). no-plus-one.undoes: C (step 9-F, F-02) — the content reaches one pixel past the client box's rounding
no-plus-one.why: jsdom does no layout, so its boxes carry no fraction past the client box; a stubbed one lands on the covered side with or without the pixel (a canvas 0.4 px wider than its client box, step 9-F, F-02)
no-plus-one.unguarded: jsdom's arithmetic lands on the covered side (a test with a canvas 0.4 px wider than its client box passed with and without it). Falsified by scripts/ruler-sync-check.mjs --mutant no-plus-one (Chromium, 2026-09-30): zoomed in 20 at the far end, Hide sidebar takes the synchronous path once; 0 without the mutant

workarea-not-observed.undoes: C (step 9-F, F-01) — the rulers read the layout again when the workarea, which centres the sheet, resizes

marks-off-pixel-grid.undoes: C (second step 10 review, R3-F1) — the marks' layers sit on whole device pixels, so a tick is painted crisp, not smeared over two; with the rounding removed the layers are placed by layout, unrounded, which is also the follow-up review's critic's probe layout-placed (CG-1)

dpr-change-ignored.undoes: C (the follow-up review, R2P-F1) — a device pixel ratio that changes with nothing resizing or scrolling puts the marks' layers on the new grid

snap-floor.undoes: C (the follow-up review, R1G-F2 and R2P-F3) — the layers go on the NEAREST whole device pixel, not the one before: rounded down, the painted 0" sits up to a device pixel before the sheet's edge

layers-half-device-px-off.undoes: C (the follow-up review, R2P-F3 and CG-4) — the layers sit ON the device grid: placed half a device pixel past it, the browser snaps them a whole device pixel from the sheet's edge

snap-against-bar.undoes: C (the review of the port, R1-F1) — the layers go on the SCREEN's whole device pixels, not the bar's: at a browser zoom (a ratio of 0.9, 1.1, 1.8, 2.2) the bars sit at a fraction of a device pixel, and a layer rounded against its bar is rounded again when painted, the painted 0" a device pixel off the sheet's painted edge (scripts/ruler-paint-check.mjs, chromium@0.9 …)

tie-rounded-down.undoes: C (the correction of the review of the port) — a reading within 1/128 of a device pixel below a half rounds up, as the browser rounds the half the sheet is laid out at: Chromium reports boxes at single precision, and a sheet at exactly 553.5 device px read back as 553.4999845 at a ratio of 2.2, so the 0" was painted a device pixel before the sheet's edge (scripts/ruler-paint-check.mjs, chromium@2.2: 3 of 30 layouts)
edits: const snap = (v: number) => Math.round(v * dpr + TIE) / dpr;
const snap = (v: number) => Math.round(v * dpr) / dpr;

transform-placed.undoes: C (the follow-up review's critic, CG-1) — the marks' layers are placed by layout, which a browser snaps to its device pixel grid when it paints, not by a script-set translate rounded the same way, which it does not snap
transform-placed.why: the unit tests read each layer's effective offset (its left or top plus any translate), which a rounded translate gives exactly as layout does; jsdom paints nothing. Measured on 2026-10-16 (record 04, section 11.3): with this mutant ruler-paint-check.mjs sees 226 of 3,078 ticks smeared in WebKit at 1.25 (27 of 30 layouts) and 121 of 3,078 at 1.5 (24 of 30), against 0 of 27,093 ticks in 265 scenarios without it; Chromium and the integer ratios paint the same either way

zoom-read-passive.undoes: C — the re-read after a zoom or gutter change runs in a layout effect, before the frame is painted
zoom-read-passive.why: jsdom renders no frames, so an effect that runs after paint is not told apart from one that runs before it
zoom-read-passive.unguarded: Looks equivalent in Chromium (the second step 10 review's critic's per-frame probe, 2026-09-30, samples taken after the rulers' own observer and at each frame): 0 painted-stale samples on Zoom in x5, Zoom out x4, Fit and two window resizes, and on Hide and Show sidebar; its positive control (the reading taken after paint) went red on Hide and Show sidebar, up to 139.7 px. The zoom commits synchronously inside the click or resize event. Firefox and WebKit not run. Again on 2026-10-16 (record 04, section 11.5): with it served, `ruler-check.mjs --frames` on the six frames-matrix scenarios (Zoom in, Zoom out, Fit, a pinch, a wheel, the window resized, the sidebar toggled, Preview left, a size change, at 1024, 1280 and 1920 px with the sidebar shown and hidden) reads 0 of 66 events stale in Chromium: no input found that shows it

onpage-passive.undoes: C — which marks are on the page is recorded in a layout effect, before any observer can read it
onpage-passive.why: jsdom renders no frames, so an effect that runs after paint is not told apart from one that runs before it
onpage-passive.unguarded: Looks equivalent in Chromium (record 04, section 11.5, 2026-10-16): with it served, `ruler-check.mjs --frames` on the six frames-matrix scenarios reads 0 of 66 events stale, over 3,151 frames. A stale record could skip a flush that a scroll or a resize needs; no input found that shows it, and nothing committed would see it if one exists (the second step 10 review's critic, C9).
